AirTag 2 launched this year with upgrades including longer tracking range and a louder speaker. However, one key feature has not been improved: battery life. The good news is that there is an accessory on the market that can extend the AirTag 2's approximately one-year battery life to 10 years or even longer.

AirTag accessory extends battery life to 10 years or more

Among the many battery-powered Apple devices, one popular product cannot be recharged: the AirTag.

The original AirTag has always been like this, and the AirTag 2 also requires a battery replacement approximately once a year.

The AirTag 2's battery life is unchanged from the previous generation. But there is a third-party accessory I really like that can dramatically extend battery life from 1 year to 10 years or even longer.

Elevation Lab's AirTag extended battery case essentially turns your AirTag into an "AirTag Max".

You simply install your AirTag 1 or 2 into the battery case (both models are compatible), insert two AA batteries, and your AirTag's battery capacity increases 14-fold.

This is both a clever and practical solution. The only downside is that the battery case makes the AirTag larger. However, I've found that most of the time, the AirTag doesn't need to be that small, so the size of the case is not an issue at all.

You can order the AirTag battery case kit from Amazon in various configurations:

Elevation Lab also offers a lighter version with 5 years of battery life instead of 10. So if the 10-year version is too bulky for you, there is another solution to consider.

An AirTag's roughly one-year battery life is actually not bad. But if you have a lot of AirTags tracking all sorts of items, getting low-battery notifications all the time can be quite annoying. If you don't mind the extra bulk from the case, I highly recommend the Elevation Lab solution.
